subject: funnel-web spider
title: Australia's Deadliest Spider Hasn't Killed Anyone in 40 Years. Why?

scenes.text: Australia's deadliest spider hasn't killed anyone in over forty years.
The Sydney funnel-web can badly poison a person within minutes, and the male's venom is up to six times stronger than the female's.
After summer rain, males wander looking for a mate. They turn up in shoes, laundry, and backyard swimming pools.
They can even survive for hours underwater, trapping a bubble of air against their bodies.
So what changed? In 1981, an antivenom made from rabbit antibodies arrived. The venom hurts people and other primates far more than most mammals.
Since that antivenom, Australia has recorded no funnel-web deaths. The deadliest spider just lost its teeth.

description:
Australia's deadliest spider hasn't killed anyone in over forty years.
The Sydney funnel-web carries a venom that can poison a person within minutes, and the male's is up to six times stronger than the female's. Wandering males end up in shoes, laundry and swimming pools after summer rain, and can survive hours underwater. An antivenom made from rabbit antibodies arrived in 1981 and no deaths have been recorded since.
Would you have checked your shoes?
first_comment: Funnel-web antivenom is still made from rabbit antibodies. Would you check your shoes if you lived in Sydney?
